Counterexample: for a Brownian motion B, M_t = exp(B_{t∧1} − (t∧1)/2) is a continuous-path test martingale whose paths have infinite total variation on [0,1] a.s. Optional stopping at τ∧1, with τ its first hitting time of 1/α, gives 1 = (1/α)·P(τ <= 1) + E[M_1; τ > 1] with the last term positive, so P(sup_t M_t >= 1/α) < α. Numerically, for α = 1/2: P(sup_{t<=1}(B_t − t/2) >= ln 2) = 1 − Φ(1.193) + ½·Φ(−0.193) = 0.3281 < 0.5 (reflection formula; a 4000-step simulation gives 0.326). Equality needs M_t -> 0 a.s. (as for Ramdas's example exp(λB_t − λ²t/2) on [0, ∞)), not unbounded total variation. The sentence also brings in continuous-time test martingales and Brownian motion, SC1 concepts outside S7's prerequisite closure (S1, S2, S3, M1-M4, CS1, P0.1, S0; curriculum.json), with no definition.
